# Pandamonium v1.0.35

Pandamonium now keeps native MCP tools available when a read-only request contains negated safety verbs. This fixes the installed acceptance failure that sent Jarvis toward generic integration tools even though MAD MCP Portal was connected and authenticated.

## MAD-842 — Integrations: make MAD MCP Portal tools native and unify connection identity

### Problem

The v1.0.34 cross-service acceptance prompt prohibited writes with the sentence “Never create, update, delete…”. Pandamonium's native MCP management detector matched `delete` without understanding the negation and treated the whole request as connection management. That skipped native MCP tool selection, left `manage_mcp` and `api_call` visible, and led the model to guess `/portal/list_services`. The Portal credential and native catalog were healthy; the generic API executor correctly refused to bypass the native MCP connection.

### Implementation

Native MCP routing is now suppressed only when the same request clause contains a connection-management action, an MCP connection target, and no preceding negation. The correction is generic and does not add Portal-specific catalogs, proxies, routes, or provider logic.

The regression uses the exact failed acceptance prompt and proves that its declared Portal discovery, reference, and read schemas reach the model-visible payload while `manage_mcp`, `api_call`, `app_api`, and `pipeline` are absent. A separate affirmative disconnect-and-delete control preserves real MCP management behavior.

### Product value and UI visibility

Read-only audits can state strict “never delete” safety rules without accidentally hiding the selected MCP server's executable tools. Jarvis can stay on the authenticated native Portal path instead of falling back to generic inventory or guessed REST endpoints. There is no visual UI change.

### Verification

The exact acceptance-prompt regression passes and confirms six declared Portal workflow schemas in the provider payload with all four generic fallbacks excluded. Adjacent MCP routing and identity coverage passes 48 tests. The complete local Python suite passes 5,535 tests with 5 intentional skips; Python compilation and diff hygiene pass. Protected PR #40 passed the full Python suite, Chromium browser tests, syntax, Compose, secrets, workflow security, dependencies, and container scanning.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, environment variable, database migration, credential, Portal server, or downstream provider change is required. The generic `api_call` guard remains intact for API credentials grouped beneath a native MCP connection. This release proves deterministic schema routing; Leo's installed CT103 update and complete configured-service acceptance remain manual and are not performed by the release workflow.
